name: FIHAN
headline: Give good work a clear introduction.
summary: A visual and verbal identity for a product built to show other products in action.
context: A product demonstration can show every screen and still leave someone wondering what the product does. FIHAN’s identity needed the same discipline as a good walkthrough: frame the useful part, guide attention and let the work make its case.
decision: The Reveal emblem combines an F with an open corner. That opening carries through the framing, iconography and motion guidance. Signal Blue draws attention; Midnight gives the interface room to breathe.
wordsWhy: Three words that give the brand a job. The supporting line, ‘Give your product a walkthrough people can follow,’ explains the benefit before the mechanism.
captions: The identity and its central promise.
The opening in the Reveal emblem becomes a recognisable device.
A deliberate division of attention, depth and breathing room.
The voice carries from a headline into everyday product messages.

name: Kepti
headline: Useful should feel approachable.
summary: A grounded identity and plainspoken voice for a conversational business ledger.
context: A shop owner should not need an accounting vocabulary to understand their own business. Kepti’s brand starts at the counter: everyday words, clear records and a calm way to draw attention to something that needs checking.
decision: Ledger green and warm paper make the system feel familiar. Saffron is a small signal for the next useful detail. The voice separates what is confirmed from what still needs checking, without talking down to the person using it.
words: Tell Kepti what happened. Know where you stand.
wordsWhy: The first sentence makes the input feel manageable. The second makes the reason to do it clear. Both stay close to the owner’s working day.
scope: Tone of voice and message patterns
captions: A conversational business companion with an orderly identity.
The foundation: capable, attentive and plainspoken.
A compact identity intended to work at the counter and on screen.
The brand expressed through words and everyday use.

name: Sapentine Interior Decor
headline: Let the finish lead.
summary: A material-led identity that brings ceilings, floors and decorative work under one clear idea.
context: Sapentine’s work spans the top of a room, the ground beneath it and the details around a building. The brand needed a way to hold those services together while keeping the actual craft in view.
decision: ‘Above and underfoot’ connects the service range in a line people can picture. Brass, plaster, charcoal and stone take their cues from the spaces themselves. The gold S emblem adds a signature without competing with the project photography.
words: A fine finish. Above and underfoot.
wordsWhy: The headline has character; the service line beneath it does the explaining. POP ceilings, floor stamping, artwork and parapet remain easy to find.
captions: A finish-led idea that connects the range of services.
The S emblem paired with a clear business name.
A palette drawn from the materials and spaces.
An expressive headline supported by practical information.

name: Proficient Electrical
headline: Confidence before the first switch.
summary: A clear, reassuring identity for electrical work, from conduits to solar installation.
context: Before electrical work begins, a customer wants to understand who they are dealing with and whether the next step will be handled carefully. The identity needed to make the trade recognisable and the business approachable.
decision: The bulb symbol establishes the category immediately. Purple and mauve retain the brand’s colour family, with a stronger name and calmer supporting typography. The guidelines carry that consistency into estimates, workwear and everyday communication.
wordsWhy: The line links the technical work to the way customers should be treated. Short, useful messages support it: explain the job, ask for the right details and make the next step clear.
captions: The light identity and its central message.
A familiar category cue and a confident business name.
Purple and mauve, used with clear roles.
Customer-facing language that sounds considered and useful.

name: MORIELA
headline: Considered, down to the last detail.
summary: A warm, craft-led direction for women’s wear, tailoring and the experience around the garment.
context: For a tailoring brand, the experience starts before a fitting and continues after the garment is collected. MORIELA’s direction connects the care in the clothes to the language, packaging and ordering details around them.
decision: Espresso, ivory and warm beige create a tactile foundation, with gold and seasonal accents used sparingly. The proposed serif wordmark aims to carry from a website header to a small garment label. The guide treats final artwork and production proofs as the next stage.
wordsWhy: A direct promise with room for personality. Supporting copy favours fit, finish and clear order details over distant luxury language.
captions: The proposed direction for the tailoring brand.
A logo system planned for large and small applications.
Warm neutrals that leave room for the garments.
The voice extends into ordering and customer care.

name: Young Gold
headline: Give colour a little discipline.
summary: A cohesive direction for a painting business with a naturally colourful identity.
context: Colour is part of the service. It can also overwhelm the message when every surface competes for attention. The Young Gold concept keeps the energy of the existing multicolour identity and gives it a more consistent setting.
decision: The playbook separates the colourful mark from the quieter layouts around it. It also organises services, photography, quote requests and field applications so the identity can be used beyond a single poster. This is a concept edition, with final artwork and details to be confirmed before production.
words: More than paint. A better space.
wordsWhy: The line starts with the service and ends with what the customer gets to enjoy. Supporting messages stay specific about surfaces, preparation and the job in question.
captions: The concept edition and its visual direction.
Working with the existing identity rather than inventing a new history.
Colour given a role and a consistent supporting setting.
A voice built around the spaces the work changes.

name: iamtaw
headline: The work has a person behind it.
summary: One recognisable identity across development, writing and the ideas that connect them.
context: My work crosses disciplines. I wanted the identity to hold them together without making me sound like a faceless studio. It needed the confidence to stand out and enough warmth to make a conversation feel natural.
decision: A custom lowercase wordmark and lime diamond tittle give the name its signature. Mulberry provides the foundation; pink brings personality; cream leaves the work space to speak. Manrope, DM Sans and an occasional italic keep the tone expressive and readable.
wordsWhy: The balance matters. The work should feel considered; the person should still come through. That principle guides the websites, the writing and the way I introduce both.

name: Nailsbyenny
headline: Let the detail set the mood.
summary: An elegant identity board built around soft neutrals, fine lettering and nail detail.
context: A beauty identity often meets someone beside the work itself: a close-up of a set, a profile picture or a booking post. This study explores a setting that feels composed without taking attention away from the nails.
decision: A fine script signature sits with blush, cream and a deep neutral. The restrained palette and delicate supporting type create a consistent mood around the imagery. The work shown is an identity board, rather than a full production-ready brand kit.
wordsWhy: Three concise cues establish the intended mood. A practical booking message would still need the service, availability and next step beside it.
captions: The original Nailsbyenny identity board.
